target_customer: Consumers in the San Francisco Bay Area booking affordable in-home massage, plus massage therapists as supply
problem: Booking a quality massage was inconvenient and expensive; the company pitched on-demand booking where and when the customer wanted.
business_model: On-demand massage marketplace taking a cut of bookings, with gift credits and a VIP membership

founders.name: Akaash Achreja
founders.background_notes: Prior role from a Crunchbase profile snippet seen in search, not opened; treat as unverified. Became advisor to Soothe after the deal.

technical_complexity.rationale: A booking and scheduling marketplace with therapist onboarding; standard web and mobile engineering with operational difficulty in supply rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplace with no sourced network effect or proprietary supply; a direct rival said it had long considered Unwind.me an acquisition target.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Soothe acquired Unwind.me in September 2015 and planned to integrate its supply-side scheduling technology.

market_need_then: Homejoy-style on-demand home services were a funded trend in 2014; Soothe reported 20 percent month over month growth and 1,700 therapists in 13 cities by September 2015, showing demand for the category.

branding.domain_note: unwind.me, a .me domain hack; unwind.com was not used.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline Homejoy for massage; Massage made simple.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches found launch listings and acquisition coverage but no press about the brand itself; many unrelated Unwind products share the name.

outcome_analysis: Unwind Me was a two person YC Summer 2014 on-demand massage startup that sold to its direct rival Soothe in September 2015 on undisclosed terms. Soothe had raised $12.3 million and was the largest massage company in the Bay Area, so the sale looks like a consolidation of a smaller competitor rather than a large outcome; the sources do not state why Unwind Me chose to sell.
notes: A $120,000 seed dated August 2014 appears only as an Xconomy headline snippet and aggregators, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round (likely the standard YC deal). Investors named by TechCrunch: 500 Startups, Slow Ventures, with YC; no amounts. unwind.me returned HTTP 503 on fetch. Zeel and traditional spas are named as Soothe's competitors in a 2015 article, not in sources dated near the batch, so competitor list is empty. Founder prior employer unverified. Failure factors are judgment from the sale to a competitor.
